assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the chemical enabling technology that turned fragile nucleic acids into deployable medicines (siRNA drugs, mRNA vaccines). The molecular design principle, pKa-tuned lipids that are neutral in circulation and charged in the endosome, gives precise control over delivery and has changed what clinicians can actually do. Originality and clarity of the chemistry are high, and impact on medicine and materials is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the foundational LNP formulation and ionizable-lipid concepts; Anderson and Langer drove combinatorial lipidoid discovery and broad delivery chemistry. MacLachlan, Hope and Madden made decisive formulation contributions, so any three-person configuration leaves out important people.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale and independently confirmed across many labs and companies. The 2023 Medicine prize recognized nucleoside modification, leaving delivery chemistry unrecognized, so timing is favorable.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among the Vancouver group, the MIT group and industrial formulators is contested and I have not verified patent or priority details.
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize topic may make some members view it as already covered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity degradation reframes drug discovery: small molecules that recruit E3 ligases to eliminate rather than inhibit a target, including previously undruggable proteins. The molecular-design logic is clear and the discovery of cereblon as the thalidomide target explained a long-standing mystery. Strong translational pull with many compounds in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target underlying molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later contributions, so the compound discovery needs a choice between the PROTAC and the molecular glue branches.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing; many clinical-stage degraders but approvals are still pending for PROTACs, so the long-term therapeutic impact is not yet fully demonstrated.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should honor PROTACs, molecular glues, or both, and who among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray is decisive.
Clinical proof of benefit for PROTACs is still emerging; thalidomide-class glue drugs have longer track record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand breaks, an elegant chemical solution that uses deaminase chemistry on DNA within a programmable scaffold. It extends the 2020 CRISPR prize chemistry and is already used in clinical settings. Originality is high and the tool changed what researchers and clinicians can do for point mutations.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear conceptual driver; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead trainees who executed the cytosine and adenine editors. Kondo and Nishida reported a related deaminase-based approach, which complicates priority but is more limited. A single-laureate configuration seems defensible.
assessment.maturity: Independent adoption is broad and first clinical results are published, but long-term safety and efficacy data are limited. Recognition may be slightly premature next to the 2020 prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as incremental on CRISPR-Cas9 recognition.
Priority between Liu and Kondo/Nishida for cytidine deamination editing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets researchers site-specifically install noncanonical amino acids in proteins in living cells using orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs. It is a foundational chemical biology capability for bioorthogonal labeling, probes, biomaterials and protein therapeutics, with wide spread across biomedicine.
assessment.attribution: Schultz pioneered orthogonal pair evolution and the first in vivo incorporation in E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended it to multiple codons and engineered ribosomes; Wang contributed early eukaryotic and mammalian work. Mehl and Yokoyama also made substantial contributions.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with two decades of independent validation and commercial use, though no single blockbuster application. Recognition is timely or even overdue.
uncertainties: Credit split between Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama is not cleanly resolved.
Perceived overlap with directed evolution and bioorthogonal chemistry prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing transformed biology and medicine, and its core is chemistry: reversible terminator nucleotides, solid-phase amplification and sequencing-by-synthesis. Impact is enormous and lasting across genomics, diagnostics and bioanalysis.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the Solexa chemistry that dominates the field; Rothberg led pyrosequencing-based 454 platform commercialization; Ju and Mayer contributed key chemistry and concepts. A Solexa-focused pair is cleanest, but a three-person list reflects competing technologies.
assessment.maturity: Mature and universally confirmed; sequencing methods were previously honored (Sanger 1980), and the Medicine and Chemistry committees may consider it already celebrated indirectly.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to credit chemistry (Solexa) over instrument commercialization (454).
Competing claims from several technology lines.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates provide a physical-chemical principle for organizing cells without membranes, connecting polymer physics, multivalent interactions and cell biology. It changed how researchers frame intracellular organization and disease, including neurodegeneration, and has spawned condensate-targeting drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated liquid-like P granules; Rosen defined multivalent-interaction phase separation in vitro. Pappu and Mittag provided the physical-chemistry framework. Credit is clear for the first three but a prize leaves out strong theory contributors.
assessment.maturity: Concept is widely adopted, but the physiological relevance of phase separation versus other assemblies is still debated in vivo, so maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Ongoing debate about in vivo evidence and rigorous definitions of condensates.
Whether this is chemistry or Medicine/Physiology territory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed nanoparticle assembly and spherical nucleic acids show how sequence-encoded recognition directs nanomaterial architecture, and led to colorimetric detection, intracellular gene regulation and clinical-stage constructs. This aligns with molecular design for precise assembly with biomedical translation, though impact on the broader field is narrower than top candidates.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin is the principal driver of both the DNA-gold assembly concept and spherical nucleic acids; Alivisatos was an independent early contributor to DNA-nanoparticle conjugates, with Storhoff and Mucic as trainees. A solo or Mirkin-Alivisatos pairing is possible.
assessment.maturity: Two-plus decades of work with commercial diagnostics, but therapeutic validation is limited and the field has partly moved to other platforms. The nanoparticle-quantum-dot prize in 2023 reduces appetite for nanomaterials.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution is a technology platform rather than a single discovery with transformative field-wide effect.
Priority between Mirkin and Alivisatos groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket turned a long-undruggable oncogene into a tractable target and led to approved drugs, built on chemical-genetics tools for kinases. This is a strong example of chemistry reaching patients, with a clear molecular design logic.
assessment.attribution: Shokat is the single decisive contributor to the KRAS G12C tethering discovery and the analog-sensitive kinase chemical genetics; drug development by pharmaceutical companies built on his work. A solo configuration is clean.
assessment.maturity: Approved drugs confirm the concept, though durability of response and resistance remain issues. The impact is clear but the discovery is relatively recent.
uncertainties: Resistance and modest clinical durability may temper perceived impact.
Industry contribution (Amgen, Mirati) to the clinical drug is not credited in this candidate.
